value.note: CORRECTED after checking Table 9. VDD's own range is UNCONDITIONAL: 'VDD Standard operating voltage, Conditions: -, Min 2, Max 3.6 V'. The widely repeated '2.4-3.6 V when the ADC is used' constrains VDDA, not VDD — Table 9 attaches footnote (1) to the VDDA row only, pointing at Table 47 Analog operating voltage for the ADC-used case. Since Table 9 note (2) requires VDD and VDDA to be at the same potential but explicitly tolerates up to 300 mV difference, they are not identical rails, so the ADC floor cannot be transplanted onto VDD. The VDDA condition is recorded on the VDDA entry in supply_rails. KNOWN LIMITATION: because supply_rails is not numerically compared, a 2.2 V board using the ADC is no longer caught by a gate; catching it would need a dedicated analog_supply_range slot plus an adc_used declaration in the requirement.

source.ref: §5.3.1 Table 9 General operating conditions, p.38 — VDD standard operating voltage 2 to 3.6 V, no conditions

value.name: VDD
value.note: Standard operating voltage, unconditional (DS Table 9, p.38). Five VDD pins on the 100-pin parts (Figure 14, p.36).

value.name: VDDA
value.note: Analog supply for ADC, reset blocks, RCs and PLL. 2.0-3.6 V with the ADC UNUSED; the minimum rises to 2.4 V when the ADC is used (DS §5.1.2 p.15; Table 9 footnote 1 points to Table 47 Analog operating voltage). Table 9 footnote 2: VDDA must be at the same potential as VDD and it is recommended to power both from the same source, but a maximum difference of 300 mV between VDD and VDDA is tolerated during power-up and operation — so they are not the same rail. May be tied to VDD through a ferrite bead for noise filtering (AN2586 §2.1, p.8).

value.name: VBAT
value.note: Supplies RTC, the 32 kHz oscillator and backup registers through a power switch when VDD is absent. With no battery fitted, connect to VDD with a 100 nF ceramic (DS §5.1.2 p.15; AN2586 §2.1 p.8).

value.name: VCORE_1V8
value.note: 1.8 V digital domain produced by the embedded voltage regulator — must NOT be fed externally (AN2586 §2.1 Figure 4 power domains, p.7; DS Figure 14 p.36).

freq_vs_supply.reason: There is no voltage-versus-frequency derating for this family: the datasheet states a single 72 MHz maximum CPU frequency across the whole 2.0-3.6 V operating range (Table 2 General features, p.10; block diagram Fmax 72 MHz, p.11). Unlike the AVR speed grades there is no table to encode, so this slot is genuinely inapplicable rather than unextracted.

value.note: HSE crystal/ceramic-resonator range. An external crystal is OPTIONAL for the core (the internal 8 MHz HSI RC can drive SYSCLK, AN2586 §3 p.12), but USB and CAN require an external clock (AN2586 §4.2 p.17 notes the boot loader needs 8 / 14.7456 / 25 MHz HSE for USB/CAN).

value.per_supply_pair_note: Each power supply pair must be decoupled with a filtering ceramic capacitor plus a chemical capacitor of about 10 uF in parallel; the capacitors must be as close as possible to, or directly below, the pins (AN2586 §6.4, p.21).

bulk.note: Minimum 4.7 uF, typically 10 uF, tantalum or ceramic. The datasheet cautions that this capacitor must be connected to VDD3 (DS Figure 14 caution, p.36); AN2586 §6.4 p.21 describes it as 'about 10 uF'.

value.placement_note: Capacitors as close as possible to, or directly below, the appropriate pins on the underside of the PCB; connections including pads, tracks and vias must be as low impedance as possible, preferably with dedicated supply planes (AN2586 §6.4 and Figure 13, p.21-22). No numeric distance is stated. VREF+ takes 100 nF + 1 uF when a separate reference is applied and must stay between 2.4 V and VDDA; it may join VDDA through a ~47 ohm resistor (AN2586 §2.1, p.8).

value.details: 'The STM32F1xx does not require an external reset circuit to power-up correctly. Only a pull-down capacitor is recommended to improve EMS performance by protecting the device against parasitic resets.' NRST has an internal pull-up RPU. The recommended capacitor value is 100 nF, which may be reduced to 10 nF to limit the power consumption of charging/discharging it through the internal resistor (AN2586 §2.2 and Figure 5, p.11). External reset needs a minimum 20 us low pulse (AN2586 Figure 5, p.11). The datasheet gives a recommended NRST pin protection circuit in Figure 31 and NRST characteristics in Table 39 (p.66-67).

value.note: BOOT1=x, BOOT0=0 selects the main flash memory as boot space — the normal application configuration. Latched on the fourth rising edge of SYSCLK after reset and resampled when leaving Standby, so the level must be held, not pulsed (AN2586 §4.1 Table 2, p.16).

On the STM32F103 BOOT1 is PB2. BOOT1=0 with BOOT0=1 boots from system memory (the built-in bootloader); BOOT1=1 with BOOT0=1 boots from embedded SRAM (AN2586 §4.1 Table 2, p.16). The 10 kOhm resistors in AN2586 Figure 11 are labelled a typical example only.

mandatory_peripherals.reason: Nothing external is mandatory to run: program memory is on-chip flash and the internal 8 MHz HSI RC can drive SYSCLK without any crystal (AN2586 §3 Clocks, p.12). USB and CAN do require an external HSE clock, but that is a per-interface requirement rather than a device-level one and is recorded in clock_external.
